question: Assume today is 2026-06-18. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate total U.S. retail and food services sales for June 2026 (seasonally adjusted and adjusted for holiday and trading-day differences, but not for price changes; a monthly amount, not an annual rate), in US dollars (the release states it in millions of dollars), as it will be first reported (advance estimate) in the U.S. Census Bureau's Advance Monthly Sales for Retail and Food Services release.

target.what: Total U.S. retail and food services sales (advance monthly estimate), seasonally adjusted and adjusted for holiday and trading-day differences but not for price changes, as first reported by the U.S. Census Bureau for the month of June 2026
target.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau (Advance Monthly Retail Trade and Food Services Survey, MARTS)
target.cadence: monthly, advance estimate released roughly mid-month following the reference month
target.caveats: Target period is future/ongoing relative to the 2026-06-18 cutoff; the June advance estimate would normally be released around mid-July 2026, after the cutoff, so no June 2026 figure exists yet. Working interpretation: nominal (not deflated) seasonally adjusted monthly total in millions of USD. Alte

candidates.hypothesis: The target is a continuation of the seasonally adjusted monthly retail and food services sales series; recent published levels (through the latest month before cutoff, e.g. April/May 2026) plus typical month-over-month growth and June seasonal factors anchor the June 2026 level.
candidates.data_to_find: Seasonally adjusted total retail and food services sales (millions USD) for each month from 2024 through the most recent month published before 2026-06-18; also the advance-vs-revised relationship and typical June month-over-month growth rates.

MARTS seasonally adjusted retail sales historical table

candidates.hypothesis: Total equals sum of published component series (motor vehicles, food services, general merchandise, nonstore retailers, gasoline stations, etc.); projecting each component and summing gives an independent route and reveals which components drive uncertainty.
candidates.data_to_find: Seasonally adjusted monthly sales by NAICS category for recent months before cutoff, with recent growth rates and June seasonal patterns for each major component.

candidates.hypothesis: Nominal retail sales growth ≈ real sales growth plus retail price inflation; CPI (goods) and PCE goods data can constrain the nominal level if a real-activity indicator is available.
candidates.data_to_find: CPI for retail goods / all items less energy for recent months, and any real retail sales or PCE goods series through the latest month before cutoff.

candidates.hypothesis: Published forecasts or nowcasts of June 2026 retail sales (e.g. from banks, forecasting firms, or the Philadelphia Fed survey) provide a direct anchor, though they may share underlying assumptions.
candidates.data_to_find: Any published forecast or nowcast of June 2026 advance retail sales (level or percent change) made on or before 2026-06-18.

candidates.perspective: High-frequency card spending and transaction data
candidates.hypothesis: Aggregate card-spending indices (e.g. Bank of America, Affinity, or Census/other transaction trackers) correlate with retail sales; a June 2026 partial-month reading can indicate direction and magnitude of change.
candidates.data_to_find: Weekly or daily card-spending / transaction indices for May–June 2026 and their historical relationship to MARTS month-over-month changes.

candidates.hypothesis: June 2026 has specific calendar features (number of weekends, holidays such as Father's Day, Juneteenth) and macro conditions (inflation, tariffs, interest rates) that shift the seasonal adjustment and level; identifying them constrains deviations from trend.
candidates.data_to_find: June 2026 calendar/trading-day structure, any major policy or price shocks (tariffs, gasoline prices) affecting retail in June 2026, and their measured or estimated impact.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
